title: Sh-K-N
hookLine: Shechinah, mishkan and shachen, neighbor: presence is neighborly

lines: A NEIGHBOR NEAR, A BROTHER FAR.
SHACHEN: THE ONE WHO DWELLS NEAR.
cards: "Better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off." That's Proverbs, and it's blunt. A brother may love you dearly.
But if he lives three states away, the one with the spare key, who notices when the mail piles up, is the person next door. The Hebrew for that neighbor is shachen: the one who dwells near.
Hold that word, because the same three letters turn up somewhere you wouldn't expect: in the Torah's word for the place God's presence lives, and in the rabbis' word for the presence itself.

teach.h: THAT I MAY DWELL AMONG THEM.
teach.b: Sh-K-N. Shin, kaf, nun. The verb shachan: to dwell, to settle, to live somewhere.
First, the tent. In the wilderness, God tells Moses: "And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them." Dwell is shachanti, from this root.
The tent they build is the mishkan, the dwelling place, the portable sanctuary carried from camp to camp. Notice the verse: not that I may dwell in it. Among them.
The tent is the address; the people are the neighborhood. Second, the presence.
The rabbis gave God's nearness a name: the Shechinah, the indwelling, the presence that settles.
In the sayings of the fathers, a teacher says that when ten sit together and study Torah, the Shechinah rests among them, and the text goes further: even two, even one.
Third, the neighbor. Shachen shares its letters with mishkan and Shechinah; dictionaries list them under one root. Whether a teacher means anything by it is up to the reader.
But some readers hear it: the word for God's presence and the word for the person next door are built the same way. So in this root, presence isn't a light in the sky.
It's someone who lives close, who stays, who can be knocked on.

how: Jews speak of the Shechinah, God's indwelling presence, resting where people gather to pray and study; the same root gives mishkan, the wilderness sanctuary, and shachen, a neighbor.

the verse says among them: the people are the neighborhood.

games.q: you need help tonight. your brother is far away; your neighbor is next door. what does Proverbs say?
o: family first, always call your brother.
better a neighbor near than a brother far off.
games.why: Proverbs is blunt: the one who dwells near, the shachen, is better than a brother far off.

practice: Picture the people who live closest to you, through the wall, across the hall, down the road, some known by name and some only by their dog or the sound of their door.
Let each come to mind for a breath, then rest on one household and think of one neighborly thing that would suit them. If you pray, you can hold that household in your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Sh-K-N. Shin, kaf, nun: the root of shachan, to dwell; mishkan, the dwelling place; Shechinah, the presence; and shachen, the neighbor. Today's word.
